Package hadur117.core.move

Class ShotModel

java.lang.Object
hadur117.core.move.ShotModel
public final class ShotModel extends Object
RAM-20: which simple aims a close-range gun really fires, learned in the battle from its bullets.

RAM-5 weighs the escape's paths against two fixed aims, head-on and linear at one fixed tick of lag. The close-range robots' guns fire a handful of variants (the one-line linear aims, circular, averaged) from a state one to three ticks old, some turning with the body, so the fixed pair often puts the bullet on the wrong side of us. This model scores every candidate aim (EXPERTS of them: the six angles of SimpleAims at each lag, and each again with the enemy's body turn added) by how near it fell to each bullet whose heading we learn (a hit on us, a bullet meeting ours), and gives the escape the TOP best as weighted rays for each new shot.

Pure and bounded: 36 doubles, no clock, no randomness. Angles are radians on Robocode's compass.

    • ready

      public boolean ready()
      Whether the model may replace the fixed aims: its leading candidate has matched MIN_SCORE bullets' worth and at least MIN_SHARE of those read. A gun none of the simple aims explains (a pattern matcher, a guess-factor gun) never clears the share, and the escape keeps RAM-5's pair against it.

    • rays

      public double[] rays(double[] aims)
      The rays a new shot is dodged as: the TOP leading candidates known for this wave.
      Parameters:
      aims - the firing wave's simple aims
      Returns:
      {angle, weight} pairs, the weights summing to 1; null when the model is not ready, the wave carries no aims, or none of the aims known for it clears the bar ready() sets
